title: Sheila E. - Wikipedia
notes: Sheila Cecilia Escovedo, born 12 December 1957, Oakland, California; daughter of the percussionist Pete Escovedo; uncle Coke Escovedo (Santana, Azteca); Tito Puente her godfather. Left Oakland High School in 10th grade to play with Azteca. Debut on Alphonso Johnson's Yesterday's Dream (1976); Solo Two (1977) and Happy Together (1978) with her father; George Duke Band percussionist 1976 to 1980 (Don't Let Go, Follow the Rainbow, Master of the Game, A Brazilian Love Affair); Herbie Hancock's Monster (1980); Marvin Gaye's Sexual Healing tour (1983). The Glamorous Life (1984), Romance 1600 (1985), Sheila E. (1987), Sex Cymbal (1991). Musical director of Prince's Sign o' the Times (1987) and Lovesexy (1988-89) tours. Ringo Starr & His All-Starr Band 2001, 2003, 2006. 'No one knows me for what I do best. But people don't realize I can play drums - I mean really play' (Los Angeles Times). Signature LP timbales with two cowbells; later a DW Collector's kit; Zildjian. Rolling Stone's 100 greatest drummers (2016): 58. Collapsed lung and a degraded calf from playing in high heels, late 1991. Bailar (2024), 'Bemba Colora' a Grammy for Best Global Music Performance.

title: Sheila E. in The Glamorous Life - Wikipedia
notes: Released 4 June 1984, Warner Bros.; produced by Prince as the Starr Company. Personnel: Sheila E. lead and backing vocals, percussion; Prince (uncredited) OB-8, DX7, piano, guitars, bass, Linn LM-1. She: 'The Glamorous Life was done in a week.'

title: The Glamorous Life (song) - Wikipedia
notes: Single 2 May 1984; US number 7, Dance number 1. Personnel (after Benoit Clerc and Duane Tudahl): Sheila E. lead and backing vocals, cowbells, timbales, cymbal; Prince co-lead and backing vocals, Oberheim OB-8, Linn LM-1; Larry Williams alto saxophone; David Coleman cello.

title: Romance 1600 - Wikipedia
notes: Released 26 August 1985, Paisley Park/Warner Bros.; recorded January-February 1985. Tracks: Sister Fate, Dear Michaelangelo, A Love Bizarre, Toy Box, Yellow, Romance 1600, Merci for the Speed of a Mad Clown in Summer, Bedtime Story. Personnel: Sheila E. percussion (all but 4), drums (1, 5, 7), Simmons SDSV (1); Prince Linn LM-1 (1, 2, 5, 6), LinnDrum (3, 4), drums (8); Benny Rietveld bass (1, 7). Live Romance 1600 filmed at the Warfield, San Francisco.

title: A Love Bizarre - Wikipedia
notes: Personnel: Sheila E. lead and backing vocals, percussion; Prince LinnDrum. She played it with Ringo Starr & His All-Starr Band in 2001, 2003 and 2006.

title: Sheila E. (album) - Wikipedia
notes: 1987, Paisley Park. Personnel: Sheila E. vocals, percussion; Timothy Riley drums; Prince drums (5), Linn LM-1 (5, 6), LinnDrum (7), Simmons SDSV (1, 10). Notable for its Latin influence.

title: Lovesexy - Wikipedia
notes: Released 10 May 1988; recorded mid-December 1987 to late January 1988 at Paisley Park. Eye No recorded with the full band (Miko Weaver, Levi Seacer Jr., Doctor Fink, Boni Boyer, Eric Leeds, Atlanta Bliss, Sheila E. on drums). Personnel (after Clerc and Guitarcloud): Sheila E. drums and percussion (1 Eye No, 2 Alphabet St., 4 Anna Stesia, 5 Dance On, 9 Positivity), backing vocals (5, 9); Prince Linn LM-1, drums, percussion. Dance On's 'machine gun-like pace'.

title: Sign o' the Times (album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 31 March 1987. Most drum sounds from the Linn LM-1. Personnel: Sheila E. Linn LM-1, cymbals, hi-hat, cowbells and timbales (U Got the Look), congas, percussion. It's Gonna Be a Beautiful Night recorded live in Paris, 25 August 1986, overdubs at Sunset Sound, 22 November.

title: Sign o' the Times (film) - Wikipedia
notes: The 1987 tour band: Cat Glover, Boni Boyer, Levi Seacer Jr., Miko Weaver, drummer Sheila E., Doctor Fink, Eric Leeds and Atlanta Bliss. Reshot at Paisley Park, the band lip-synching to the concert recording; Eric Leeds: around 80% of the film from the reshoot. 'Drum solo by Sheila E.'

title: Robyn Flans, 'Sheila E.', Percussive Arts Society Hall of Fame
notes: At 15 she subbed for her father's sick percussionist in Azteca (touring from 1973); later recorded and toured with George Duke, Herbie Hancock and Billy Cobham. Learned by watching her father in a mirror image, so she played left-handed on right-handed congas: the timbales set up left-handed and the cowbells right-handed, 'they're both switched'. Influences: her father's Latin and Latin jazz, salsa, Motown, Sly and the Family Stone, Tower of Power, Santana, the Grateful Dead, classical training, gospel. DW built her mics inside the timbales and hydraulic stands. Stopped drumming in heels after nerve damage. 'You have to open yourself up to being versatile and playing other genres of music.' First Latina percussionist/drumset player in the PAS Hall of Fame.

title: 'Die besten Drummer der Welt: Sheila E. - The Queen Of Percussion', Bonedo
notes: German. Plays the drumset right-handed, congas left-handed after her father. 'I am a percussionist who plays percussion on drums - I'm not the drummer who plays percussion.' 'I try to play from my heart.' Early influences Harvey Mason, Karen Carpenter, Billy Cobham, Tito Puente. Kits: 1986 a red Yamaha Recording Custom, two bass drums, Ludwig Black Beauty 14x5, Paiste 2002; 1987-88 a turquoise kit with Simmons pads triggering Linn sounds and a Roland Octapad; 1991 (Modern Drummer) Yamaha Rock Tour Custom, Yamaha brass piccolo snare, Paiste Signature, Remo Pinstripe; later DW, five pieces, a 20-inch bass drum, Zildjian; a DW Icon 13x5.5 signature snare; LP timbales, Toca cowbells. Lovesexy: drums on five songs, a drum solo on the tour. Sex Cymbal's 808 Kate, a one-minute drum solo.

title: Sheila E. Teaches Drumming and Percussion, MasterClass (2020)

title: Songsterr 5489882: Sheila E. - The Glamorous Life, drums (rev 8443383, by James, 2026)
notes: Human (aiGenerated false); the earlier revision 7177053 is machine-made. 4/4 at 128, 120 bars: eighths on the hat, the snare on 2 and 4, the kick on 1, the 'a' of 2 and the 'and' of 3 (81 bars); the hat in sixteenths (bars 61-65, 86-90); the kick on the 'and' of 1 (96-100). The record's drum machine part; no timbales.

title: Sign o' the Times (1987), Sheila E.'s drum solo; and Prince, Housequake, Paisley Park, 31 December 1987
notes: Footage looked at frame by frame: a big kit, two bass drums, Paiste cymbals, pale turquoise shells (clearest in the Paisley Park New Year's Eve video, YouTube em6h7OhEdQY); she plays it right-handed in a black sleeveless top. Tempos beat-tracked from the records: Glamorous Life 127.5, Sister Fate 125.8, Eye No 112.0, Alphabet St. 104.1, Anna Stesia 99.9, Dance On 124.9, Positivity 105.6, the film's Housequake 125.9.
